conventions.convention: The integers d,n are positive. Ω is a nonempty bounded connected open subset of Euclidean space with locally smooth graph boundary. Smoothness on its closure means restriction from an open neighborhood of the closure.

The target consists of complex positive definite Hermitian n-by-n matrices with determinant one. The dagger is conjugate transpose, trace is the finite diagonal sum, J=Φ⁻¹dΦ, and divergence is the sum of coordinate derivatives of the current components.
The comparison uses Ψ=Φ₁Φ₀⁻¹−I and ΔJ=J₁−J₀; the Laplacian is the positive-coordinate-sum convention Δ=Σ∂ₐ². Uniqueness requires equality on the entire boundary.

The Lorentzian signature is (−,+,+,+). A stationary field is specified and timelike only on a specified nonempty open subset. Axial symmetry is a supplied effective smooth isometric U(1) action, parameterized with period 2π, with spacelike generator away from its fixed-point axis.

Circularity means local integral surfaces for the rank-two distribution orthogonal to the supplied generators on U*, where those generators are independent and their span is nondegenerate. U* may be empty; commutation and circularity are not assumed.

The matrix comparison is an abstract Euclidean deduction. No stationary electrovacuum uniqueness, stability, cosmic-censorship result, or empirical conclusion follows without separate hypotheses and arguments.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated smooth positive Hermitian determinant-one matrix solutions on Ω, Δ tr Ψ = Σₐ tr((ΔJₐ)† Φ₁ ΔJₐ Φ₀⁻¹) ≥ 0. If Φ₁=Φ₀ on the entire boundary, then Φ₁=Φ₀ on the closure.

For smooth Φ from the closure of the specified bounded Euclidean domain into positive definite Hermitian determinant-one matrices, define J=Φ⁻¹dΦ and the matrix harmonic-map equation div J=Σₐ∂ₐJₐ=0 on Ω.

Supplies the stationary field, effective isometric circle action, axis, nondegenerate two-generator domain U*, orthogonal rank-two distribution, and local immersed-integral-surface definition of circularity; neither commutation nor circularity is inferred.
